title: Remark
body_md: Note that Problem~\eqref{eq:comb-opt} is analogous to the \emph{least trimmed squares} estimator~\cite{Rousseeuw1984,Rousseeuw2006LTS} which is known to be robust to strong contamination~\cite{bhatia2015robust,Bhatia2017Consistent}, in i.i.d. regression. However, unlike the standard \emph{least trimmed squares},  problem~\eqref{eq:comb-opt} involves products $z_t  z_{t+1}$ and is thus formulated as a quadratic program w.r.t. $(z_t)_{t=1}^T$.
head: environment

title: Remark
body_md: We assume $s$ is known a priori, following \cite{diakonikolas2019effi, diakonikolas2023near, diakonikolas2024robust, RobustLin2025, pensia2021robust}.
head: environment

title: Remark
body_md: The convergence of Algorithm \ref{alg:robust-estimator} will depend on the initialization $A^{(0)}$. Since the relaxations considered are all non-convex, while a choice of $A^{(0)}$  within a small neighborhood of the ground-truth might lead to convergence, its unclear whether this holds for any random initialization. In practice, a potential choice of $A^{(0)}$ is to solve the $\ensuremath{\mathcal{A}}$-constrained least squares problem on the contaminated data -- our experiments follow this strategy.
head: environment

label: rem:solve-A
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{rem:solve-A}
Suppose we fix $z \in \left\{{0,1}\right\}^T$. Then \eqref{eq:sphere} is essentially just $\ensuremath{\mathcal{A}}$-constrained weighted least squares which is the same as solving \eqref{eq:quad-form} (with fixed $z$). For \eqref{eq:biconvex}, we can replace $b_t$ with $z_t  z_{t+1}$ (which is what the envelope constraints would be doing) and therefore, it reduces to solving \eqref{eq:quad-form} with fixed $z$. For \eqref{eq:SDP} if we set $Y = zz^\top$, then $\Big\langleQ(A),Y\Big\rangle = z^\top Q(A) z$ which for fixed $z$ is the same as \eqref{eq:quad-form}. Solving \eqref{eq:quad-form} over $\ensuremath{\mathcal{A}}$ takes $O(n^2T+n^3)$ time for $\ensuremath{\mathcal{A}} = \ensuremath{\mathbb{R}}^{n \times n}$, and $O(n^2T+n^3K)$ for $\ensuremath{\mathcal{A}} = \left\{{A \in \ensuremath{\mathbb{R}}^{n \times n}: \big\|{A}\big\|_{1,1}\le \big\|{A^*}\big\|_{1,1}}\right\}$ (with $K$ iterations of the FISTA algorithm \citep{beck2009fast}).
head: environment

title: Remark
body_md: In this work, we consider one of the simplest forms of filtering (with $D$). In the i.i.d. robust regression setting, works such as \cite{sasai2024outlier, pensia2021robust} use more sophisticated approaches, including iterative filtering and weight learning. Extending these to the VAR setting is not straightforward as the dependence between data would break the concentration arguments underlying their analyses.
head: environment

title: Remark
body_md: The estimator \eqref{eq:l12-ls-pen} is analogous to the penalized lasso that has been well-studied for robust sparse regression with i.i.d inliers (e.g., \cite{dalalyan2019outlier,sasai2020robust,chen13Robust}).
head: environment

label: rem:impl-LS
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{rem:impl-LS}
 
In the experiments, where we focus on $\ensuremath{\mathcal{A}}$ as in \eqref{eq:Astar_l1ball}, we solve \eqref{eq:l12-ls-pen} via a combination of block coordinate descent and constrained weighted least squares via alternating minimization in $O((n^2T+n^3K)\widetilde{K})$ time for $\widetilde{K}$ iterations (where $\widetilde{K}$ is small in practice).   \eqref{eq:spr-ls-hard} is solved via alternating minimization. Indeed, when $A$ is fixed then $U$ can be solved for exactly by picking the columns of $(\bar{Y}-AY)D$ with the largest $\ell_2$ norms, which can be computed in $O(nT \log T)$ time by computing the norms and sorting. When $U$ is fixed, we revert to $\ensuremath{\mathcal{A}}$-constrained weighted least squares which can be solved efficiently (as described above) in $O(n^2T+n^3K)$ time (see Remark~\ref{rem:solve-A} for specifics on $K$).

body_md: The stated error bound holds for $T$ suitably large. When $s \leq \log(n/\delta)$ then $T \gtrsim k^2 \log^4(n/\delta)$ suffices. label: def:talagrand-gamma
title: Definition
body_md:
\label{def:talagrand-gamma}
Let $(\ensuremath{\mathcal{M}},d)$ be a metric space. We define an adimissible sequence to be a sequence of subsets of $\ensuremath{\mathcal{M}}$, $(\ensuremath{\mathcal{M}}_r)_{r \ge 0}$, where $\ensuremath{\left | \ensuremath{\mathcal{M}}_0 \right |} = 1$ and $\ensuremath{\left | \ensuremath{\mathcal{M}}_r \right |} \le 2^{2^r}$ for all $r \ge 1$. For any $0 < \alpha < \infty$, the $\ensuremath{\gamma_{\alpha}}$ function of $(\ensuremath{\mathcal{M}},d)$ is defined as,
\[
\ensuremath{\gamma_{\alpha}} (\ensuremath{\mathcal{M}},d) \coloneq \inf \sup_{s\in \ensuremath{\mathcal{S}}} \sum_{r=0}^{\infty} 2^{r/\alpha} d(s,\ensuremath{\mathcal{M}}_r)
\]
where the $\inf$ is over all admissible sequences of $\ensuremath{\mathcal{M}}$.
